governing_question: Can this signal earn and keep the right to influence capital allocation?

hypotheses.source_claim: Newly available U.S. House and Senate bill language, especially legislation that has just completed congressional passage, may contain policy alpha when its legal and economic implications are strong enough to support a specific trade.
hypotheses.decision_information: The official final-chamber passage timestamp, the exact operative text version agreed to by both chambers, and only official fiscal, committee or agency material publicly available before the policy-impact memo is sealed.
hypotheses.target_instrument: U.S.-listed common stocks and sector or industry ETFs with at least USD 10 million of median daily dollar volume over the prior 20 regular sessions, mapped before entry.
hypotheses.entry_rule: Within 120 minutes after the later of final congressional passage and public availability of the operative text, seal a versioned policy-impact memo using no post-event price information. Enter the mapped long and short exposures at the next regular-session open after the memo timestamp.
hypotheses.exit_rule: Primary exit is the fifth regular-session close after entry. Record 1, 20 and 60-session outcomes as secondary diagnostics without selecting the best horizon after observing results.
hypotheses.direction_rule: Long exposures whose expected cash flows, capital access, legal permissions or demand are directly improved; short exposures whose expected cash flows, costs, legal permissions or demand are directly impaired. Record no trade when direction is not unambiguous before entry.
hypotheses.trigger_rule: Every event must pass all five pre-entry gates: final congressional passage in identical operative form; a direct binding economic mechanism; a pre-entry company or subindustry exposure mapping; quantifiable materiality from contemporaneously available official information; and implementation or binding effect expected within 24 months.
hypotheses.benchmark: The matching sector or industry ETF, or an equal-weighted unaffected same-subindustry peer basket, selected and sealed in the policy-impact memo before entry.
applicable_regimes: all final-congressional-passage events that pass the five-part tradeability gate
fiscal, tax, tariff, subsidy, procurement, regulatory, sanctions and export-control mechanisms reported separately
invalid_regimes: operative text unavailable before the memo is sealed
nonbinding, ceremonial or purely naming measure
target-specific earnings, merger or other material issuer news between the prior close and entry
official action timestamp cannot be verified
hypotheses.cost_model: Use recorded opening and closing spreads and slippage when available; otherwise apply a predeclared conservative equity and ETF execution schedule, plus commissions and observable stock-borrow cost for short positions.
hypotheses.deactivation_rule: Deactivate after at least 30 untouched eligible events if benchmark-adjusted after-cost expectancy is non-positive, or immediately if official timestamps, operative text, policy-impact memos or pre-entry exposure mappings cannot be reproduced without post-event information.
hypotheses.out_of_sample_boundary: Events whose final congressional passage occurs on or after 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z are out of sample. Earlier events are reconstruction and development data only.
hypotheses.timezone: UTC for legislative events and storage; America/New_York for U.S. regular-session execution
hypotheses.bar_size: legislative event study with next-open entry and regular-session close exits
hypotheses.source_fidelity_notes: The earlier semiconductor and federal-equity framing was one example, not the intended universe. This canonical version deliberately begins with objectively observable just-passed legislation. The about-to-pass pre-passage idea remains an enhanced blocked variant until its probability, amendment-risk and timing rules are frozen.

hypotheses.source_claim: Bills that are about to pass may create a tradable policy-information advantage before final congressional passage.
hypotheses.decision_information: Near-final bill text, official chamber schedules, committee or leadership actions, and other passage evidence that was public before any proposed entry.
hypotheses.target_instrument: The same liquid U.S.-listed common-stock and ETF universe as the canonical post-passage version.
hypotheses.exit_rule: A future frozen version must use predeclared exits that can be compared directly with the canonical 1, 5, 20 and 60-session horizons.
hypotheses.benchmark: The canonical signal benchmark plus a matched sample of scheduled votes that failed, were delayed or changed materially.
applicable_regimes: officially scheduled final-chamber consideration
near-final legislative text with limited amendment risk
invalid_regimes: material text amendment after signal formation
passage probability inferred after observing the market reaction
hypotheses.deactivation_rule: Reject the pre-passage extension if passage-event selection, text finality or amendment risk cannot be determined prospectively and reproduced from archived public information.
hypotheses.timezone: UTC for legislative evidence and America/New_York for execution
hypotheses.source_fidelity_notes: The user's broader goal explicitly includes bills that are about to pass. It is preserved here, but canonical-before-enhanced prevents it from being frozen until the simpler post-passage version is tested and the pre-passage selection rules are objective.

hypotheses.source_claim: Timestamped public Apple campaigns by the tracked account may contain directional skill.
hypotheses.decision_information: The first public post that clearly initiates or reverses an AAPL directional campaign; later scaled entries remain part of the same campaign.
hypotheses.target_instrument: AAPL common stock; options are excluded from the canonical version.
hypotheses.entry_rule: Enter at the next AAPL regular-session open after the qualifying post. A pre-open post uses that day's open; an intraday or after-hours post uses the next regular-session open.
hypotheses.exit_rule: Primary exit is the fifth regular-session close after entry. Also record 1, 10, 20 and 60-session outcomes as secondary diagnostics without selecting the best horizon.
hypotheses.direction_rule: Long for an unambiguously bullish campaign and short for an unambiguously bearish campaign.
hypotheses.trigger_rule: A post must contain an unambiguous AAPL direction and a timestamp available before entry. Ambiguous, deleted-without-archive, or non-executable posts are recorded but not traded.
hypotheses.benchmark: QQQ return over the identical entry-to-exit interval; SPY and raw AAPL returns are secondary controls.
applicable_regimes: all regimes for the primary test
large-cap technology
options-driven positioning
hypotheses.cost_model: Use recorded opening and closing bid-ask spreads when available; otherwise apply a predeclared conservative equity spread/slippage schedule equally to long and short campaigns, plus borrow cost for shorts.
hypotheses.deactivation_rule: Deactivate after at least 30 untouched eligible campaigns if benchmark-adjusted after-cost expectancy is non-positive, or immediately if posts cease to be timestamp-verifiable and executable.
hypotheses.out_of_sample_boundary: Campaigns first posted on or after 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z are out of sample. Earlier campaigns are reconstruction and discovery data only.
hypotheses.timezone: America/New_York for AAPL sessions; source timestamps also preserved in UTC
hypotheses.bar_size: campaign event with regular-session entry and close exits
hypotheses.source_fidelity_notes: The source concerns public calls, but the exact five-session stock implementation is a deliberately simple research definition. Options performance is deferred until the stock version works.

hypotheses.source_claim: A 90-period Hull moving average may improve trend participation or reduce adverse exposure.
hypotheses.decision_information: The completed UTC daily close and the Hull moving average calculated only from closes available through that timestamp.
hypotheses.entry_rule: Enter long at the next UTC daily open when the prior daily close is above HMA(90) and HMA(90) is higher than its prior value.
hypotheses.exit_rule: Exit at the next UTC daily open after either the prior close is at or below HMA(90), or HMA(90) is not higher than its prior value.
hypotheses.direction_rule: Long-only. Shorting and multi-asset application are enhanced variants and are not part of version 1.
hypotheses.trigger_rule: Both price-above-HMA and positive-HMA-slope conditions must be true on a completed daily bar.
hypotheses.benchmark: BTCUSDT buy-and-hold over the complete test interval and a simple SMA(90) rule using identical execution assumptions.
applicable_regimes: all regimes for the primary test
persistent trend as a predeclared subgroup
hypotheses.cost_model: Apply historical exchange fees where available plus a predeclared spread and slippage schedule at every next-open execution.
hypotheses.deactivation_rule: Deactivate if the rolling 50-trade after-cost expectancy is non-positive or if the data source can no longer reproduce the frozen daily bars.
hypotheses.out_of_sample_boundary: Bars opening on or after 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z are out of sample. Earlier bars are development data.
hypotheses.source_fidelity_notes: The source did not fix asset, timeframe, or trigger. Version 1 intentionally chooses one liquid asset, one daily timeframe, and a long-only rule so the simple version can be tested before expansion.

hypotheses.source_claim: Bitcoin may react predictably around monthly VWAP, potentially near month-end.
hypotheses.decision_information: Completed hourly BTCUSDT perpetual bars and monthly VWAP reconstructed from trades since 00:00 UTC on the first calendar day of the month.
hypotheses.entry_rule: Enter long at the next hourly open after the first hourly close above monthly VWAP that follows at least one hourly close below monthly VWAP during the prior six completed hours.
hypotheses.exit_rule: Exit at the earlier of 24 completed hours after entry or the next hourly open following an hourly close below monthly VWAP.
hypotheses.direction_rule: Long-only reclaim. Touch-bounce, rejection shorts, adaptive bands, and month-end filters are enhanced variants.
hypotheses.trigger_rule: A valid reclaim requires a completed below-VWAP close within six hours and then a completed above-VWAP close; no future volume or bars may enter the VWAP calculation.
hypotheses.benchmark: Matched BTCUSDT perpetual 24-hour returns beginning at the same UTC hour on non-signal days.
applicable_regimes: all liquid BTC regimes for the primary test
month-end as a predeclared subgroup
invalid_regimes: trade-history gap preventing exact VWAP reconstruction
hypotheses.cost_model: Use historical maker/taker fees according to the assumed market order, bid-ask spread, slippage, and realized funding over the holding interval.
hypotheses.deactivation_rule: Deactivate if the rolling 50-signal after-cost expectancy is non-positive or if exact monthly VWAP cannot be reproduced from source trades.
hypotheses.out_of_sample_boundary: Signals entered on or after 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z are out of sample. Earlier signals are development data.
hypotheses.source_fidelity_notes: The source did not define touch, reclaim, or exit mechanics. Version 1 freezes the simplest one-sided reclaim rule and defers all additional variants.

hypotheses.source_claim: Consumer-discretionary risk appetite may lead Bitcoin in some liquidity regimes.
hypotheses.decision_information: The completed XLY and SPY regular-session closes for a U.S. trading day.
hypotheses.entry_rule: At 16:05 America/New_York on each XLY trading day, enter BTC in the sign of XLY's same-day excess return over SPY.
hypotheses.exit_rule: Exit at 16:00 America/New_York on the next XLY trading day.
hypotheses.direction_rule: Long BTC when XLY minus SPY daily return is positive; short BTC when it is negative; no trade when it is exactly zero or either close is unavailable.
hypotheses.trigger_rule: Use only official completed XLY and SPY regular-session closes. No magnitude threshold is used in the canonical version.
hypotheses.benchmark: Unconditional BTC return over identical holding intervals and a SPY-sign control rule.
applicable_regimes: all regimes for the primary test
macro liquidity expansion
risk-on/risk-off rotation
invalid_regimes: late or corrected official close unavailable by entry
hypotheses.cost_model: Apply BTC perpetual taker fees, bid-ask spread, slippage, and funding for the exact holding interval.
hypotheses.deactivation_rule: Deactivate if XLY excess-return sign adds no positive rolling 100-observation after-cost expectancy beyond the SPY-sign control.
hypotheses.out_of_sample_boundary: Entries on or after 2026-08-03T16:05:00-04:00 are out of sample. Earlier observations are development data.
hypotheses.timezone: America/New_York for signal timing; UTC preserved in storage
hypotheses.bar_size: one U.S. trading day predictor and next-trading-day BTC holding interval
hypotheses.source_fidelity_notes: Version 1 tests the simplest lead claim using the sign of XLY excess return. Thresholds, constituents, rolling beta, and longer lags are enhanced variants.

hypotheses.source_claim: Late Korean semiconductor-market movement led SNDK's following U.S. session during a temporary June-July 2026 regime.
hypotheses.decision_information: KOSPI 200 index level at 23:30 America/New_York and its immediately preceding official KRX close, both known before the following SNDK regular session.
hypotheses.entry_rule: Enter at the following SNDK regular-session open after the 23:30 America/New_York KOSPI 200 observation.
hypotheses.exit_rule: Exit at that same U.S. session's regular close.
hypotheses.direction_rule: Long SNDK when the KOSPI 200 change from its prior official close to 23:30 America/New_York is positive; short SNDK when negative; no trade when zero or unavailable.
hypotheses.trigger_rule: The KOSPI 200 observation and prior close must be timestamp-verifiable before the SNDK open. SNDK-specific material news between observation and entry is recorded as an invalidating event.
hypotheses.benchmark: SOXX open-to-close return on the same U.S. session; raw SNDK open-to-close return is also retained.
applicable_regimes: June-July 2026 discovery regime
future periods tested separately without assuming the regime persists
hypotheses.cost_model: Use opening and closing spread/slippage, commissions, and observable stock-borrow cost for short signals.
hypotheses.deactivation_rule: Keep capital rights at none and mark the signal inactive whenever the rolling 20-observation after-cost relation is non-positive or the claimed cross-market lag cannot be reproduced.
hypotheses.out_of_sample_boundary: Observations whose SNDK entry occurs on or after 2026-08-03 are out of sample. June-July 2026 is discovery data only.
hypotheses.timezone: America/New_York with source exchange timestamps preserved in UTC and Asia/Seoul
hypotheses.bar_size: one overnight predictor observation and one U.S. regular session
hypotheses.source_fidelity_notes: The chart measured SNDK from 23:30 to the next close, but a 23:30 SNDK entry is not assumed executable. Version 1 deliberately translates the claim to the next regular-session open and records the difference from the source chart.

hypotheses.source_claim: BTC, ETH, SOL and HYPE may rebound before U.S. equities after a common risk dip.
hypotheses.decision_information: Only prices available through each one-hour decision bar, with asset-specific trailing volatility capped at 30 bars.
hypotheses.target_instrument: BTC, ETH, SOL and HYPE versus ES, NQ, a MAG-7 basket and a semiconductor basket
hypotheses.entry_rule: This is initially an ordering study rather than a trade entry rule. For each predeclared shock, record the first timestamp each asset satisfies each rebound component.
hypotheses.exit_rule: End observation when every asset reaches full rebound, the predeclared maximum event horizon expires, or the event is invalidated.
hypotheses.direction_rule: Crypto leads when its predeclared unweighted component timestamps occur before the corresponding equity timestamps; no volatility-weighted aggregate is permitted in version 1.
hypotheses.trigger_rule: Evaluate local-low reversal, reference reclaim, trend confirmation and sustained recovery using the existing frozen component formulas.
hypotheses.benchmark: Null distribution from predeclared common-shock events with asset labels permuted and from matched non-event drawdowns.
applicable_regimes: common macro risk dip
synchronized crypto and equity drawdown
invalid_regimes: event declared after observing the recovery ordering
hypotheses.cost_model: Not applicable to the ordering study; any later trading translation must model each instrument separately.
hypotheses.deactivation_rule: Reject the lead hypothesis if it does not survive untouched common-shock events or if event selection cannot be made without outcome knowledge.
hypotheses.out_of_sample_boundary: Begins only after the common-shock detector and maximum event horizon are frozen.
blocking_fields: exact unweighted basket timestamp aggregation rule
hypotheses.source_fidelity_notes: All four rebound components and the short volatility lookback are preserved. The signal remains blocked because selecting dips after seeing which asset recovered first would create look-ahead bias.

hypotheses.source_claim: BTC showed negative median returns before month-end and positive median returns after the month boundary in the supplied 30-month chart.
hypotheses.decision_information: The known UTC calendar boundary and BTCUSDT perpetual quotes available at execution time.
hypotheses.entry_rule: Enter long at 00:05 UTC on the first calendar day of each month.
hypotheses.exit_rule: Exit at 00:05 UTC exactly seven calendar days after entry.
hypotheses.direction_rule: Long-only post-month rebound. The pre-month short and symmetric two-leg strategy are enhanced variants and are not part of version 1.
hypotheses.trigger_rule: Every eligible month boundary is included; no leverage, funding, open-interest, VWAP, quarter-end, or prior-return filter is permitted in the canonical version.
hypotheses.benchmark: All non-overlapping seven-calendar-day BTCUSDT perpetual returns beginning at 00:05 UTC, with weekday composition reported separately.
applicable_regimes: all liquid BTC regimes for the primary test
quarter-end and leverage regimes as predeclared subgroups only
invalid_regimes: exchange outage around entry or exit
hypotheses.cost_model: Use BTCUSDT perpetual taker fees, bid-ask spread, slippage at entry and exit, and realized funding for the full seven-day hold.
hypotheses.deactivation_rule: Deactivate if the rolling 12-month after-cost expectancy is non-positive or if the effect fails the first untouched 12 eligible month boundaries.
hypotheses.out_of_sample_boundary: Month boundaries on or after 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z are out of sample. The 2024 through July 2026 chart period is discovery evidence only.
hypotheses.source_fidelity_notes: The source chart included several before/after windows. Version 1 freezes the simplest long-only seven-day post-month rule and defers the short leg and conditional filters.
